pages.title: Muster — the race to the cogosseum

content.value:
# Muster

AI generals command armies across a world of floating sky-island arenas arranged in concentric rings. Each general builds an economy (mine, farm, barracks, refinery), raises a military, fights for territory and glory, and sails INWARD ring by ring toward the cogosseum at the center.

## What you can submit

A policy can drive any of three layers — it's your local training choice, and all three compete in the same league:

- **General** (macro): build order, recruiting, diplomacy, combat commands, and the dock → shipyard → transport → launch-inward race. This is the `coworld_pkg.player.player` entrypoint (the bundled default).
- **RL soldier** (per-unit micro): the engine ships each unit's observation + action masks + role in the protocol's `soldier_obs` batch, and your policy returns per-unit `{move, target, mode}` actions. Entrypoint `coworld_pkg.player.soldier_player` (the bundled v34 numpy soldier paired with a heuristic general).
- **Hybrid** (both): drive the general AND the soldiers in one policy.

See the player protocol doc for the wire format of both channels.

## How an episode resolves

An episode is a bounded epoch of the whole world. At the tick budget, the CHAMPION is the seat that is in the cogosseum and alive with the most glory (fallback: top glory overall). Per-seat results report glory, territory, kills, whether each seat reached the cogosseum, and whether it survived. **The outer ring CRUMBLES on a timer** — linger on a starter island too long and your army is destroyed, so racing inward is survival, not just upside.

The core thesis: entertainment is the optimal strategy. Glory comes from theatrical play — flanks, comebacks, tide-turns — so boring agents starve and entertaining agents thrive.

game.name: Muster
game.description: A spectator hex-RTS coworld: AI generals command armies across a world of floating sky-island arenas, racing inward through the rings to the cogosseum. A submitted policy can drive the GENERAL (macro: economy, military, diplomacy, sailing inward), the per-unit RL SOLDIERS (micro: movement, targeting, retreat), or BOTH (hybrid) — the protocol carries a general-action channel AND a per-unit soldier_obs batch. One episode is a bounded epoch of the multi-arena world; the champion is the seat that reaches the cogosseum alive with the most glory. Entertainment is the optimal strategy — boring agents starve, entertaining agents thrive.

seed.description: Deterministic episode seed — same seed reproduces a byte-identical world.

tokens.description: Connection tokens. config_schema requires a FIXED maximum, so this caps at 64 = MAX_COMPETITION_SEATS, the empirically reliable hosted-pod ceiling (the brain's binary search found N>76 fails at job setup; 64 ships with headroom). 64 is the MAX number of REAL policies one episode can seat — NOT the world size: the world is ~96 island-armies, and the GAME ENGINE scripted-fills every seat beyond the real ones. The custom MusterCommissioner decides how many are REAL per episode (qualifier=1, competition=the division's champion count, min 2, up to 64). The runner injects these.

version.description: Optional policy-authored version or artifact label.

policy_id.description: Stable cross-episode policy identity. When absent, replay evidence uses an honest episode-scoped external-slot id.

controller_kind.description: Declared implementation kind. Muster never infers LM or RL from channel traffic.

players.description: Display-name objects, one per REAL policy slot a variant uses (1 for the qualifier, up to 64 = MAX_COMPETITION_SEATS for competition). The engine scripted-fills the rest of the ~96-army world.

max_ticks.description: Bounded epoch length in decision ticks; the champion is crowned at this tick.

tick_rate.description: Decision ticks per second for live viewing (does not affect the deterministic outcome).

num_agents.description: Deprecated commissioner-compat seat hint (VariantInfo.num_agents). Does NOT constrain the roster: infer_token_count ignores it, so the competition variant still seats the variable real-champion count the commissioner sends. Present only so the platform's _compat_variant_num_agents can resolve a concrete count for a players-omitted variant.

num_arenas.description: Number of arenas in the ring topology (cogosseum + outer rings). The full league world is 19 — the `default` competition variant's value; the qualifier load-check uses 2 (cogosseum + one starter island). Minimum 2 because a 1-arena world would seat the lone army in the fight-to-death cogosseum with no starter island.

isQualifier.description: When true, this episode is the Qualifiers division's connect/build/run/score LOAD-CHECK (the tiny `qualifier` variant), NOT a competitive match. The engine uses it to take the cheap path — no inward-race / ring-crumble pressure, which only matters at full scale. Competition variants omit it (or set false).

episode_timeout_seconds.description: The REAL wall-clock budget (seconds) for one episode, read by the commissioner framework to set its per-episode duration limit (limit = max(300, 2 x this)). MUST be set for any multi-minute episode: otherwise the framework infers the budget as max_ticks/tick_rate — which treats tick_rate as real-time pacing (for Muster 750/50 = 15s) and floors the limit at 300s, CANCELLING the real episode ('Episode job duration exceeded 300 seconds'). Set this to the episode's true expected wall-clock so the full game runs to completion.

player_connect_timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for all player slots before starting anyway.

llm_drove.description: True only if >=1 LLM call succeeded AND >=1 decision was driven by model text.

llm_endpoint.description: AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME when the platform Bedrock sidecar is in play.

llm_failure_kinds.description: auth | model_access | throttle | timeout | quota | other:<Code> -> count.

llm_model_answered.description: The model id that ACTUALLY answered (the chain may fall forward on a model-access failure).

llm_fallback_reason.description: VERBATIM provider text of the FIRST failure, prefixed by kind and model id.

llm.description: Did an LLM actually drive this episode? `llm_drove` is the headline; when it is false, `llm_fallback_reason` names the cause in the provider's own words. Written by src/agents/lm/llm_telemetry.py.

banked.description: Whether each seat banked its glory (all-or-nothing scoring: unbanked glory is forfeited on a wipe).

champion.description: Winning seat (0..95), or -1 if no seat survived to be crowned.

exemplars.description: Per-seat behaviour EXEMPLARS (additive, optional — lane P 2026-08-17): the episode's best deeds / peak-glory tick / elimination moments, each carrying tick + arena + a one-line what-happened so a replay viewer can deep-link the moment (the Logs contract: every event row deep-links to a replay tick). Derived from the artifact's glory_ledger + recorded eliminations joined through the seat's (arena, team) trail.

outcomes.description: War outcome kind -> count (elimination | withdrawal | truce | separation | arena_end | episode_end | unresolved), the war ledger's own histogram. NEVER summed across kinds — shapes differing by a discriminator are different KINDS (2026-08-17 law). Empty object when wars_opened == 0.

wars_won.description: Per-seat count of wars the seat's warband won — scoped to the unambiguous case only: outcome kind == elimination AND the seat's side was not the eliminated side. Truce/withdrawal/separation are not credited as a win to either side.

available.description: Did the war-ledger compiler run this episode without error? False means every other field above is the zero fallback, not a measurement.

wars_closed.description: Wars whose outcome kind != episode_end — i.e. the fight actually concluded (by whatever kind) before the episode ended, as opposed to still being hot at the horizon.

wars_opened.description: Count of wars that opened this episode.

betrayal_turns.description: Treachery beats (alliance_broken with betrayal:true) recorded INSIDE a tracked war's window, summed across wars. Excludes bond-decay breaks (reason: withered|strain) — a rotting alliance is not a stab in the back; the war ledger keeps these split and this field only ever counts the treachery side.

combat_effects.description: Raw combat_effect count fed to the war compiler this episode — distinguishes a genuine zero-war episode (combat_effects > 0, wars_opened == 0) from a channel that never fired (combat_effects == 0).

largest_war_seats.description: Total belligerent warbands (both sides combined) in the episode's single largest war, 0 if no war opened. Counts every warband in the war, not only submitted-policy seats — the biggest fights are often scripted-fill vs scripted-fill.

wars_participated.description: Per-seat count of wars the seat's warband was a belligerent in, same seat order as `scores`/`glory`/`kills`.

war_summary.description: Compact per-episode WAR summary (lane war-ledger-public, 2026-08-17), compiled from the war-ledger channel (muster.war-ledger.v1 — sustained conflicts reified from causal_events/arena_events/world_events/team_bindings). Without this field, wars existed ONLY inside the live server's .replay bundle and never reached results.json / the public league page. Follows the `llm` block's own pattern: unconditionally emitted, `available=false` means every other field is the zero fallback, not a measurement — never confuse a real zero-war episode with a channel that didn't run.

seat_metrics.description: Per-seat learning aggregates at LIVE tempo (additive, optional — lane P 2026-08-17): reward_mass_by_layer over the FULL term vocabulary (a 0.0 layer is the dead/farmed-layer finding), realized_norm_entropy per action head (collapse detector; realized-behaviour entropy, NOT policy output entropy), action_histograms (general action types + soldier move/target/mode), mask_legality_mean, and behaviour roll-ups (engagement rate, spread, focus-fire share, approach flips, whiff fraction, flanks/ambushes/saves, rout survival).

glory_by_deed.description: Per-seat record channel (additive, optional — lane K 2026-08-17): deed name -> summed minted glory from the episode's glory ledger, so a 0.0 pinball score still carries the story of what the warband earned before it was wiped. Derived from the artifact's glory_ledger channel by the seat's stable global_id.

behaviour_tags.description: Per-seat auto-tags for the named pathologies (additive, optional — lane P 2026-08-17): passive_camp, deathball, whiff_storm, disengage_loop. Every tag row carries its measured value, the calibrated threshold, and the sample support — tags are arguable evidence, never bare verdicts. Thresholds calibrated against scripted personality references (tools/probe_behaviour_calibration.py).

control_ledger.description: Per-seat CONTROL ATTRIBUTION (additive, optional — lane P 2026-08-17): per decision tick, who actually controlled the seat — general channel policy/noop(missed window)/scripted/absent counts + general_fallback_frac, soldier channel policy/autopilot/no_units/inactive/absent counts + units offered/driven. Without this, an episode the policy drove 3% of and one it drove end-to-end score identically; no league score attributes to the policy. The full per-tick timeline rides the replay artifact's control_timeline channel.

forfeited_glory.description: Glory each seat forfeited by dying unbanked.

reached_cogosseum.description: Whether each seat reached the cogosseum (ring 1).

player.name: Muster Default General
player.description: Creds-free heuristic general mirroring Muster's scripted-general priorities: mine-first economy, concentrate fire on the lowest-HP enemy only when locally favorable, then run the full naval chain (dock → shipyard → escorted transport → launch inward toward the cogosseum). A COMPETENT-BUT-BEATABLE baseline — held to the strong scripted general's level, not a weak shadow — and the default a submitted optimizer is expected to beat.

player.name: Muster RL Soldier
player.description: Trained per-unit RL soldier micro (the v34 hybrid multi-head policy, run as a dependency-light numpy forward pass) paired with the bundled heuristic general. It exists to DEMONSTRATE the RL-soldier submission shape — the engine ships each unit's observation + action masks + role in the per-seat protocol's soldier_obs batch, and this policy returns per-unit move/target/mode actions — NOT as a co-equal winner: the soldier fights its units well, but as a whole-army driver at full scale it underperforms the bundled general (it doesn't drive economy/the inward race), so it is a SHAPE EXAMPLE, not a strong baseline. A submitted policy image can drive the general, the soldiers, or both (hybrid).

variants.name: Full Muster world — every champion, one shared game (19 arenas)
variants.description: The full 19-arena Muster world (~96 island-armies). EVERY submitted champion the Competition division has plays in ONE shared episode; the engine scripted-fills every remaining island-army. This variant deliberately OMITS a baked players[] list, so the seated real-policy count is whatever the commissioner sends that round (verified: infer_token_count→None → the platform seats len(policy_version_ids) and game_config_with_named_players builds exactly that many players; tokens schema stays variable 1..64). As more policies qualify, more real slots + more islands fill in — some partially, some fully — with NO per-size variants and no re-ship. Capacity ceiling 64 real (hosted-pod limit); beyond that the commissioner windows across full episodes. episode_timeout_seconds=600 (→1200s limit) keeps the full multi-minute episode off the max_ticks/tick_rate 300s floor. Ring 3 present → the ring-crumble fires; racing inward is survival.

variants.name: Qualifier load-check (1 seat, 2 arenas)
variants.description: A minimal load-check used only by the Qualifiers division: ONE connected policy on a tiny 2-arena world (its ring-2 starter island + the cogosseum) for a short 80-tick epoch. It is NOT a competitive match — it just proves the submitted policy connects, builds, runs without crashing, and scores, before it enters real (full-world) competition. (1 arena would seat the lone army directly in the fight-to-death cogosseum, so 2 is the minimum that gives it a normal starter island to play.) isQualifier=true tells the engine this is the cheap load-check path — no inward-race / crumble pressure needed at this scale (with only ring 2, the ring-crumble can't fire anyway). The full 19-arena world is the `default` variant used by the Competition division.

commissioner.name: Muster League Commissioner
commissioner.description: Custom Muster commissioner (ruleset_strategy base + per-division variant selection) running a FLAT ladder — no Bronze/Silver/Gold tiers, no promotion/relegation. The Qualifiers staging gate runs the tiny `qualifier` variant (1 seat / 2 arenas / 80 ticks) as a fast connect/build/run/score LOAD-CHECK that can't hit the 300s episode cap; any policy that completes it is promoted once into the single Competition division and stays there. Competition runs the full `default` 19-arena world, seating EVERY real champion the division has (min 2 to start a round, up to MAX_COMPETITION_SEATS=64) while the engine scripted-fills the rest of the world. Each round persists its own glory scores; the separately stored division standing ranks each player's all-time high. Rounds run every 15 minutes.
